area: tasks import --force erases the active claim without being asked to
finding: tasks import --write --force resets the ledger record to status planned and drops the active claim even when --force-overwrite-claims is not passed. The existence of that separate flag is the system's own statement that --force alone must not displace claims. Recovery costs three further governed commands: tasks repair-claim to diagnose, tasks repair-claim --write to release the orphaned runtime lock, and next --claim to retake the task.
expectedBehavior: Refreshing a ledger record from its planning card updates the record's declared fields. Claim state is not a declared field of the planning card, so it must survive the refresh. Displacing a claim requires --force-overwrite-claims and must emit the claim-displaced-by-import transition event that already exists for exactly this purpose.
evidenceOrRepro: On ATM-GOV-0360, two import --force runs under emergency lease EMG-ATM-GOV-0360-cbdda3e03f each left status=planned and claim=undefined in .atm/history/tasks/ATM-GOV-0360.json while the runtime lock survived, so the following next --claim failed with ATM_LOCK_CONFLICT and needed tasks repair-claim --write before the task could be retaken. The transition log for the card records the full sequence: import, import, reserve, promote, repair-claim, claim.
followUp: Resolved by ATM-GOV-0364 in commit b5bf02d16e2e837b3533596b31d9a284133dbc57. The preservation branch existed but was gated on parseClaimRecord returning a fully-formed record, so a claim that was live but missing an optional field read as no claim at all. It is now gated on hasPreservableClaimState, which asks about the claim's state rather than its shape: any claim state other than released or empty is preserved. Regression guard: test_atm_gov_0364_import_refresh_preserves_its_own_claim in tests/cli/governance-round-trip-cost.test.ts. The distinct claim-identity aggregate defect remains open in [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-017]. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-007], which is what forces the import --force in the first place.
